panels.description: Just before dawn inside the Keel pump hall. Alex Phantum, eighteen, with brown skin, short dense black curls, dark eyes, lean build, scarred work-rough hands, dark rolled-sleeve work shirt over a black tee, rust-brown patched cargo trousers, heavy scuffed boots and a worn canvas backpack hanging from one straight shoulder strap, presses one palm flat to an aging pump housing. A salvaged bracket replaces the approved part. A projected maintenance procedure and white-and-amber Alpha node sit to one side. The supervisor watches with folded arms. Leave the upper third open for dialogue.

End-of-shift checkpoint. Alex places his hand on the scanner while non-recognizable workers queue behind him. Danny, lanky with a buzz cut and open grin, stands ahead. A large dedicated administrative display fills the right half of the panel with generous vertical line spacing. Keep the left third clear for BEEP, the guard, Alex and the caption; no lettering crosses the interface.

Morning street outside THE LAST CHANCE — PAWN & LOANS and NEXT LEVEL GAMES. The shopkeeper stands in the loan-shop doorway beside used goods and Adrian’s torn default notice. Danny emerges with a used console and game-shop bag, waving a printed loan slip. Across the street, non-recognizable people queue at a public tap. Keep the shop sign at upper-left, Danny’s balloon in upper-center, the loan slip beside Danny and the ration sign at far right, each in a separate clear zone.

At left, the supervisor alone in the pump hall selects ROUTINE MAINTENANCE beside the blinking Alpha node and scratched balanced water-drop mark. At right, Alex stands on the pit rim before the sealed mine entrance, looking toward sunlit Oasis while Keel remains in shadow. Reserve separate upper zones for the procedural balloon and Alex’s line, and two separated bottom caption boxes.

items.text: Eighteen: the age Keel decides you're old enough to owe.

items.speaker: DANNY
items.text: Alex! Look what I got! Ten a week. That's nothing!

items.speaker: SHOPKEEPER
items.text: Care to see if your luck runs better than his?

items.speaker: SHOPKEEPER
items.text: Your father always believed the next loan would change everything.
ADVANCE 120 CR · REPAY 10 CR / WEEK · 31 WEEKS
Everyone in Keel knew where they had been born.
Few believed they could choose where they belonged.
